title: Hom-colimit criterion for an essentially constant pro-diagram
statement: Let $J$ be a cofiltered category, $\mathcal C$ a category, and $G:J\to\mathcal C$ a diagram. Suppose there are an object $X$ of $\mathcal C$, an index $j_0$ of $J$ and a morphism $r:G(j_0)\to X$ such that for every object $W$ of $\mathcal C$ the map $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,W)\to\varinjlim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(G(j),W)$, $\varphi\mapsto$ the class of $\varphi\circ r$ at the index $j_0$, is a bijection. Then $G$ is essentially constant as a pro-object with value $X$ in the sense of [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram]; its cone maps $u_j:X\to G(j)$ are characterized by: the class of $u_j\circ r$ at $j_0$ equals the class of $\mathrm{id}_{G(j)}$ at $j$ in $\varinjlim_{k}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(G(k),G(j))$, and they satisfy $r\circ u_{j_0}=\mathrm{id}_X$.

source.place: Categories, Lemma Tag 05PY, implication (4) => (1), pro-object case (dual of the ind characterization)

proof.text: For each object j of J, apply the assumed bijection with W=G(j) to the colimit class represented by id_{G(j)} at j. Let u_j:X\to G(j) be its unique preimage. If a:j\to j' is a morphism of J, postcomposition by G(a) carries the class of id_{G(j)} to the class of G(a) represented at j and also carries the class of id_{G(j')} to that same class. Naturality of the assumed bijections in W and injectivity therefore give G(a)\circ u_j=u_{j'}, so (u_j) is a cone.

source.place: Categories, Lemma Tag 05PY, implication (4) => (1), construction of the cone maps in the pro-object case

proof.text: With W=X, naturality under postcomposition by r shows that the image of r\circ u_{j_0} under the assumed bijection is the class of r represented at j_0. The image of id_X is also that class, because the defining map sends id_X to the class of id_X\circ r=r at j_0. Injectivity gives r\circ u_{j_0}=id_X.

source.place: Categories, Lemma Tag 05PY, implication (4) => (1), retraction clause in the pro-object case

proof.text: Fix j. By the definition of u_j, the class of u_j\circ r represented at j_0 equals the class of id_{G(j)} represented at j in the relevant filtered colimit. Equality of two representatives in a filtered colimit of sets means that there is an object k with morphisms k\to j_0 and k\to j for which their pullbacks agree. Thus the transition G(k)\to G(j) equals the composite G(k)\to G(j_0)\xrightarrow{r}X\xrightarrow{u_j}G(j).

source.place: Categories, Lemma Tag 05PY, implication (4) => (1), factorization clause in the pro-object case

proof.text: The cone (u_j), the index j_0, the morphism r, the identity r\circ u_{j_0}=id_X, and the factorization established for every j are exactly the data and clauses in the definition of an essentially constant pro-object with value X. The construction also gives the stated characterization of each u_j, namely that the class of u_j\circ r at j_0 is the class of id_{G(j)} at j.

lean.statement: theorem homColimit_essentiallyConstantProDiagram {J : Type uJp} {C : Type uCp} [Category.{vJp} J] [Category.{vCp} C] [IsCofiltered J] (G : J ⥤ C) (X : C) (j₀ : J) (r : G.obj j₀ ⟶ X) (h : ∀ (W : C), Function.Bijective (fun φ : X ⟶ W ↦ ((G.op ⋙ yoneda.obj W).ιColimitType (Opposite.op j₀) (r ≫ φ)))) : IsEssentiallyConstantProDiagram G X ∧ ∃ (u : (Functor.const J).obj X ⟶ G), u.app j₀ ≫ r = 𝟙 X ∧ (∀ (j : J), (G.op ⋙ yoneda.obj (G.obj j)).ιColimitType (Opposite.op j₀) (r ≫ u.app j) = (G.op ⋙ yoneda.obj (G.obj j)).ιColimitType (Opposite.op j) (𝟙 (G.obj j)))
lean.note: Uses the recorded IsEssentiallyConstantProDiagram and Mathlib Functor.ιColimitType for the quotient colimit of G.op ⋙ yoneda.obj W; independent universes need no smallness or HasColimit hypothesis. The cone legs are uniquely determined by the displayed identity-class equation, by h injectivity.
